extracted.intended_audience: military administrators, Judge Advocate General staff, and War Department officials responsible for civilian employee policy and discipline
extracted.subtask_description: Digest of legal rulings and departmental guidance governing civilian employees of the military establishment (leave, holidays, pay stoppage, travel, details, resignation/discharge, compensation, definitions, and related personnel rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility for leave
rubrics_metrics.description: Which civilian employees are entitled to leave.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes expert accountant, Inspector General's Department staff, employees of navy yards, gun factories, naval stations, arsenals, armories, ordnance and powder depots; excludes employees of inspectors of ordnance on duty at works not belonging to the United States.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nature and limits of leave (annual and sick)
rubrics_metrics.description: Amounts and aggregate limits of paid leave available to civilian employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thirty days' annual leave and 30 days' sick leave may be granted; more than a total of 60 days' leave with pay may not be granted in any one year even if absence caused by sickness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surgeon's certificate and absence without leave
rubrics_metrics.description: Effect of medical certificate on pay when employee is absent without leave.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In case of absence without leave, a surgeon's certificate does not automatically restore pay, though it may guide the Secretary of War in acting on the case (discretionary).

rubrics_metrics.name: Leave when presence jeopardizes others' health
rubrics_metrics.description: Granting leave because an employee's presence would jeopardize fellow clerks' health.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Leave may be granted for this reason but total paid absence in the year must not exceed 60 days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secretary of War detailing clerks as military instructors
rubrics_metrics.description: Authority to detail clerks to military instructor duty without deduction of time or pay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Secretary of War may not detail a clerk of the War Department as military instructor at a school without deduction of time or pay (no statutory authority to do so).

rubrics_metrics.name: Indefinite leave without pay for volunteer service
rubrics_metrics.description: Authority to grant indefinite leave without pay to cover absence as officer of volunteers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No authority exists for granting indefinite leave without pay to a clerk to cover absence while serving as an officer of volunteers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lay-offs and continuity of service for leave
rubrics_metrics.description: Effect of authorized lay-offs on continuity of service for accrual of leave.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time lost by employees due to lay-offs by proper authority does not interrupt the continuity of service for leave purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hiring temporaries to cover employees on leave without pay
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding and propriety of hiring temporary employees to replace those absent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proper expenditure for the Quartermaster's Department to use funds to procure temporary employees to replace employees at large who are absent on leave without pay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Per diem employees: entitlement to holiday pay
rubrics_metrics.description: When per diem (day-paid) employees are entitled to pay for holidays.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Per diem employees may enjoy State-established holidays but not receive pay for them in some cases; they may receive pay for holidays established by law unless employment ended the day before or began the day after such holiday; pay allowed for specified joint resolution holidays (Jan 1, Feb 22, July 4, Dec 25) only when those dates do not fall on Sunday except special rule for July 4; the joint resolution of 1887 (Memorial Day, Fourth of July) applies beyond Washington, D.C., and to per diem and permanent employees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspended per diem employees and holiday pay
rubrics_metrics.description: Pay entitlement for suspended per diem employees during periods including a holiday.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Per diem employees suspended and not at work during a period that includes a holiday are not entitled to pay for that holiday.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment for work on holidays: double pay prohibition
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether employees who work on holidays can receive double pay.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employees who work on holidays are not entitled to double pay absent an express statute authorizing the same.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pay stoppage: private debt and other restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: Limits on withholding or stopping pay from civilian employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pay of a civilian employee cannot be stopped to liquidate private indebtedness to an enlisted man; however, the commanding officer of an arsenal may stop pay to the extent necessary to make good damage to government property caused by the employee's neglect; hospital charges due to the United States from civilian employees may be collected from sums subsequently found due them; pay may be stopped to meet excess of leave taken under a prior appointment when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jury duty and similar civil obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Calling officers and civilian employees for jury duty or road work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It is generally held they should not be called upon because of required duty to the United States, but the question is for the courts to decide in each case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pay while absent as a witness
rubrics_metrics.description: Entitlement to paid leave when absent to serve as a witness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employees covered by the act of 1898 are not entitled to leave with pay while absent as witnesses except when summoned as a witness for the United States; employees not covered by that act are entitled to leave with pay while absent as witnesses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions of civilian status and related offices
rubrics_metrics.description: Classifications: who is a civilian employee, what counts as civil officer vs military.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Crew of a transport are civilian employees; superintendents of national cemeteries are civil officers of the United States but not part of the military establishment and are not entitled to military allowances; master mechanic at an arsenal is employment, not a Federal office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Holding other offices while in civil employment
rubrics_metrics.description: Permissibility of accepting other offices while employed as a civilian clerk.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A civil service clerk may not accept appointment as vice consul of a foreign power even with no salary attached; a clerk may not accept office as alderman or city attorney; quartermaster employees are not prohibited by statutes/regulations from accepting office as a member of a city council.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notary public fees for clerks
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether clerks who are notaries may take fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A clerk who is also a notary public is not precluded from receiving statutory notary fees in executing contracts with the Government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Details: assignment and eligibility for certain duties/offices
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules on detailing enlisted men and clerks to particular duties or positions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An enlisted man may not be detailed for clerical duty in the Quartermaster's Department (forbidden by act of Aug 5, 1882), but may be so detailed in the office of the Chief of Artillery; clerks provided under the 1894 appropriation are not eligible for appointment as post noncommissioned staff officers; clerks provided for headquarters may be assigned to duty with the Artillery Board at Fort Monroe (restriction is to details to Bureau duties).

rubrics_metrics.name: Travel and transportation expenses for clerks
rubrics_metrics.description: When travel and related expenses may be paid for clerks or personal clerks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No precedent for allowing traveling and other expenses of the personal clerk of an officer ordered before a court of inquiry; if the clerk is a material witness he may be subpoenaed and paid witness fees; transportation for postal clerks ordered 'for duty with troops in the field' was held payable from Army transportation appropriations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on additional/dual compensation
rubrics_metrics.description: When extra compensation can or cannot be paid to government officers/clerks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutes (secs. 1763-1765 R.S.) restrain the Executive from giving dual or extra compensation intended to cover all services of an office; they prevent extra pay for added duties that are part of the same office unless special legislation authorizes it. However, two distinct offices or employments, each with its own duties and compensation, may be lawfully held by one person and paid separately. Example: a disbursing clerk could be paid from the Gettysburg National Park appropriation for distinct duties performed for that Commission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clerks appointed under appropriation acts: protections
rubrics_metrics.description: Status and protections of clerks appointed under specific appropriation acts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under the appropriation act of Aug 6, 1894, clerks and messengers provided are to be employed and apportioned by the Secretary of War; department commanders have no power to discharge them or to increase or reduce their salaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acting chief clerk compensation limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Authority (or lack thereof) to pay additional compensation to acting chief clerks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An application for additional pay as compensation for services performed as acting chief clerk cannot be allowed except by authority of Congress (secs. 1764 and 1765 R.S.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Resignation acceptance and effective date rules
rubrics_metrics.description: When resignation may be accepted and its effective date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resignation may be accepted to take effect upon the last day the employee worked, even if acceptance is communicated later; where a civilian accepts employment with no understanding as to tenure, he may resign when he sees fit; acceptance of resignation follows similar rules to officers—after due notice of acceptance is communicated, there can be no withdrawal or revocation. A resignation tendered by a civil-service employee under investigation for political activity should not be accepted; the employee should be dismissed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discharge: effect and irrevocability
rubrics_metrics.description: Legal effect of discharge and whether it can be converted to resignation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ultimate discharge of an employee as of the date of his suspension is lawful; a clerk discharged for cause may not be allowed to resign in lieu of discharge; a legally executed discharge is beyond recall even if there was mistake on the part of recommending or issuing officers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Injuries: compensation under May 30, 1908 act
rubrics_metrics.description: When compensation for injuries to civilian employees is payable and what it may include.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Under the act of May 30, 1908, compensation may include commutation of rations if subsistence was furnished the employee at time of the accident; relief under that act was denied in certain contexts (e.g., injury while working on bridge connected with water supply in one cited case).

rubrics_metrics.name: Military service status of civilian employees
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether civilian employees serving armed or in wartime become military.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clerks who, in 1862, were 'employed as an armed force' remained civilians and were not in military service; the term 'service in war' in uniform regulations relates to service as an officer or enlisted man and does not attach to the status of a civil employee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Desertion rule for civilian employees
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether abandoning civilian employment can create liability similar to desertion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A civil employee does not become liable as a deserter by abandoning his employment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seaman discharged abroad: wages and public charge
rubrics_metrics.description: Rights of a seaman discharged by voluntary consent in a foreign port and limits on discharge in foreign ports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a seaman is discharged by voluntary consent in a foreign port he is entitled to wages up to time of discharge; unless his time has expired he should not be discharged in a foreign port to become a public charge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Miscellaneous prohibitions and administrative practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Other issued rulings and examples clarifying permissible and impermissible acts by civilian employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include: a War Department clerk acting as treasurer of a society making personal loans at 2% per month violated an executive order of April 13, 1911; civil service rules permit appointment without examination of a second driver for the Secretary of War in certain cases; when a commissioner for marking graves died while in office, the Chief Clerk of the War Department should certify remaining vouchers.
